evals.prompt: I just joined the team and keep hearing about this AI-SDLC thing and the /sdlc command. Can you explain how the whole system works? I learn better with diagrams.
evals.expected_output: A layered explanation (idea → flow → decisions) that reads the ai-sdlc source files, leads with a mind map and a phase flowchart, names the real phases/statuses/gates as they exist in source (not from memory), and highlights the human approval gates. Should NOT hardcode a phase count or agent list without deriving from source.
assertions: Contains at least one Mermaid diagram (```mermaid fenced block)
Leads with a visual (mind map or phase flowchart) before deep prose
Names actual pipeline phases consistent with commands/sdlc.md (no invented/wrong phase set)
Explicitly surfaces the human approval gates (plan/design/promotion pauses)
States the principle that the orchestrator coordinates but never does the work itself
Does not assert a hardcoded phase/agent count that contradicts the source

evals.prompt: Give me a Mermaid diagram of the /sdlc pipeline flow, including the loops where work gets sent back.
evals.expected_output: A Mermaid flowchart with one node per phase in the order found in commands/sdlc.md, including back-edges (bug loop, plan-challenge loopback, failed-merge route) and annotated human gates. Phases derived from source, not invented.
assertions: Output contains a valid Mermaid flowchart block
Has one node per pipeline phase in the order found in commands/sdlc.md
Includes back-edges/loops (bug/defect loop and/or plan-challenge loopback), not just the happy path
Annotates at least one human approval gate on the flow
Phase names match the source rather than being invented

evals.prompt: I want to add a new agent to the ai-sdlc pipeline. Before I touch anything, walk me through how the system is structured so I don't break the way the agents coordinate.
evals.expected_output: A contributor-level explanation: the Jira message-bus coordination contract, the one-artifact-per-phase discipline, the spawn protocol, agent anatomy, worktree isolation, and where the source of truth lives — with file:line citations. Derived from the conventions skill and orchestrator, not from memory.
assertions: Explains the Jira-as-message-bus + one-artifact-per-phase coordination contract
Explains the agent spawn protocol (general-purpose Agent, pointer-not-body, model tier)
Includes file:line or file-path citations to the actual source
Points to where source of truth lives (orchestrator + agent files + conventions skill)
Does not fabricate coordination rules absent from the source
